title: Integrals & accumulation

review.interaction: implemented; numerical fixtures are not independent mathematical review

source_policy: Definition-level references support the mathematics. Applications and stories are original constructed scenarios, not measurements or historical events. Historical claims require claim-level sources before publication.
purpose: Recover a traveled distance by accumulating a changing velocity.
meaning: Each thin time slice adds a little distance. The whole shaded area connects instantaneous speed to the cart’s position.

research_tasks: Research the concept and notation with specialist sources before adding historical attribution.
history.reader_text: Historical account not yet sourced. Everyday scenarios are constructed examples, not historical anecdotes.

examples.title: A cart from rest
examples.question: How far does a cart travel in 4 s at constant acceleration 2 m/s²?
examples.setting: Original constructed teaching scenario; stipulated quantities are not measurements.
assumptions: The cart starts from rest at position zero.
Acceleration is constant and positive; motion remains along one forward axis.
Time is nonnegative and the stated units are consistent.

steps.reason: Find the velocity at the end of the interval.

examples.interpretation: The instantaneous final speed is 8 m/s; the accumulated distance is 16 m.

independent_check.method: A separate algebraic rearrangement or frequency-table check.
independent_check.expected: Average velocity is (0+8)/2=4 m/s; 4 m/s × 4 s = 16 m.

examples.limits: The cart starts from rest and acceleration remains constant.
conditions_to_check: The cart starts from rest at position zero.
Acceleration is constant and positive; motion remains along one forward axis.
Time is nonnegative and the stated units are consistent.

steps.reason: The shorter interval reduces both triangle width and height.

examples.interpretation: Halving the elapsed time quarters the traveled distance in this model.
